question: How do I structure a partner/channel motion alongside direct sales?
answer:
**Direct Answer:** Run channel separate from direct sales (different comp, different territories, different SKUs). Partner CAC is typically 2–3x lower than direct; partner NRR is 15–25% lower. Launch channel at $5–10M ARR with dedicated partner manager. Target channel to drive 20–30% of ARR by year 3. **The Detail** Channel partners (resellers, consultants, integrators) multiply reach but require different mechanics than direct sales. **Why separate teams matter:** | Dynamic | Direct AE | Channel Partner | Conflict | |---------|-----------|-----------------|----------| | Commission | 15–30% | 20–35% (need higher margin) | Partner wants bigger discount | | Territory | Named accounts | Geographic/vertical region | Partner encroaches on direct | | Support | CSM owned by Vendor | Partner-delivered (varies in quality) | Poor partner execution kills NRR | | Pricing | Standard list | Distributor tier (30–40% discount) | Partners undercut direct deal prices | | Customer relationship | Vendor owns buyer | Partner owns buyer (vendor is "ghost") | Partner locks in customer, leaves you | **Channel segmentation by size:** | Partner Tier | ACV They Drive | Quantity | Who Manages | Notes | |--------------|----------------|----------|-------------|-------| | Strategic (Tier 1) | $200k–$500k+ | 3–5 partners | VP Channel | Integrators, system implementers | | Mid-Tier | $50k–150k | 10–20 partners | Partner Manager | Regional resellers, consultants | | Affiliate | $5k–30k | 100+ partners | Automated tools | SaaS aggregators, affiliate networks | **Channel-only SKU/pricing structure:** Don't let partners sell your core SKU (they'll discount to 50% off). Instead: **Core Direct SKU:** - List: $100/user/mo - Direct discount: 10–20% - Direct effective: $80–90/user/mo **Channel Partner SKU (different product tier or packaging):** - List: $80/user/mo (30% lower to give partner margin) - Partner gets: 30–35% discount → costs them $52–56/user/mo - Partner sells for: $70–75/user/mo (15–35% margin) - Customer pays: 25% less than direct (price justification: implementation by partner) **This prevents channel from cannibalizing direct sales.** **Partner program economics (18-month model):** **Phase 1 (Months 1–6): Recruit and onboard** - Hire 1 Partner Manager ($80k + overhead = $120k fully burdened) - Target: 3–5 Tier 1 strategic partners - Spend: $40k (partner enablement, co-marketing, training) - Expected revenue: $0 (pipeline building phase) - Cost: $160k **Phase 2 (Months 7–12): Generate pipeline** - Partners generate 5–10 deals (mostly validation, not revenue yet) - Support: ongoing enablement + co-selling - Cost: $120k - Expected ARR: $300k–400k (deals close in month 12) **Phase 3 (Months 13–18): Scale** - 3–5 Tier 1 partners now producing, add Tier 2 - Expected new logos: 20–30 - Expand Partner Manager role (now needs junior counterpart) = +$80k - Cost: $200k - Expected ARR: $800k–$1.2M **Total 18-month investment: $480k** **Projected ARR by month 18: $1M** **Payback: ~18 months** (but ongoing channel revenue scales faster after payback) **Partner comp structure:** **Reseller (owns customer):** - First-year: 30% of ACV (paid at deal close) - Year 2+: 15% of renewal (annual, declining 5% per year) **Managed Service Partner / Integrator:** - First-year: 20% of ACV + 5% implementation fee (customer pays, partner executes) - Year 2+: 5% of renewal - Implementation risk: Partner absorbs 50% of overruns **Affiliate / Referral:** - One-time: 5–10% of first-year ACV - No renewal commission (affiliate role is passive) **Channel conflict management (critical):** 1. **Territory exclusivity rules** — Define: "Partner X owns financial services vertical in EMEA; direct sales owns companies >$100M revenue in EMEA." 2. **Partner vs direct pricing gap** — If partner charges less than direct, direct loses confidence. Max acceptable gap: 15%. 3. **Deal registration** — If prospect is sourced by partner, partner gets discount (and deal is locked to partner). If direct closes prospect already in partner's vertical, dispute resolution: split commission 50-50 or direct gets 100% (depends on agreement). 4. **NRR accountability** — Partners historically have 70–85% retention (worse than direct 90%+). Build into SLA: - Partners must hit ≥85% retention or lose Tier 1 status - If partner has <5 customers, NRR SLA waived (statistical insignificance) **Metrics to monitor:** - Partner-sourced new logos: Target 20% of total new business by month 18 - Partner NRR: Should track separate from direct (expect 10–20% lower) - Partner CAC: Should be 40–60% of direct CAC (that's why you do channel) - Partner deal cycle: Usually shorter (90–120 days vs 180 days direct mid-market) - Partner engagement: Monthly co-selling calls, quarterly business reviews ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Launch Channel
